transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Start time: 15:00 PT (PDT)
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jillian Park (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Tara Singh (Oxbridge Head of ML), Michael O'Connor (Platform Eng), Priya Raman (SRE)

Summary:
- Quick Q4 check-in focused on cost spikes from peak inference, p99 latency regressions after recent release, and roadmap tradeoffs for a private/VPC pilot.
- Agreed to benchmark mixed hosted/dedicated routing and produce two pricing scenarios.
- Next steps: benchmarks, pricing scenarios, SOC2 contacts, schedule deep-dive on private deploys.

Topics discussed:
- Current usage profile and anomalies
- Latency & p99 regressions after recent prompt expansions
- Cost run-rate and reserved capacity tradeoffs
- Private deployment (VPC, KMS) constraints and timeline
- Rollout strategy: canary vs sized dedicated pools and fallback policies

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jillian: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jillian from Redwood, AE on the account. We have Marco here from solutions engineering. How are you all doing?
[00:08] Tara: Good, thanks. Busy quarter, but ready to dig in.
[00:11] Michael: Hey, hi, everyone. Quick note we're on a compressed agenda cause we have the exec sync at 4:30.
[00:17] Marco: Totally fine. We'll keep the high level first and then dive.
[00:20] Jillian: Cool. Quick frame: we want to cover the usage spike you saw last week, the p99 latency climb, and a proposed mix of hosted plus dedicated routing to control costs. Tara, do you want to start with the spike context?
[00:34] Tara: Yeah. So last Thursday we saw a 3x token volume spike, mostly from our Summarize+Enrich pipeline. There's a new experiment that increased avg sequence length, and that seems to have driven CPU/GPU lockups -- or sorry, not lockups, but queueing and p99 jumped like from 220 ms to 1.1 s.
[00:52] Michael: To add, the traffic shape is bursty — a lot of small requests plus periodic large ones. Our current routing is hosted only. We haven't committed to Dedicated yet because the ops team is nervous about over-provisioning cost.
[01:06] Marco: Understood. A few clarifying Qs: what's your typical seq len distribution and token counts per minute during normal vs spike? That matters a lot for kernel selection, batching behavior and KV cache effectiveness.
[01:19] Tara: Normal: 60-100 tokens. Spike: 400-1,200 tokens on the enrich path. Tokens per minute during spike hit 35k TPM vs baseline 12k. I'll share the CSV after this call.
[01:32] Marco: Perfect. That explains batching saturation and the p99 regression. Our runtime makes different kernel choices based on seq length; at >512 you get a different code path that can be more expensive. Also be aware prefix/KV cache usefulness drops if requests are more diverse.
[01:49] Jillian: On cost we saw your bill jump ~2.8x for that week. We proposed two pricing scenarios in the deck — a hosted-heavy with autoscale and pay-as-go, and a blended reserved model with a small dedicated pool to handle peaks.
[02:02] Priya: The cost spike is concerning but we also need reliability. If we go dedicated, we need VPC + KMS and audit logs. That's mandatory for our compliance team.
[02:14] Jillian: Totally. For the private/VPC option we can support customer-managed KMS and long retention audit logs. Marco can walk the architecture afterwards.
[02:21] Marco: Yep. Roughly the private flow: dedicated instances in your VPC, private endpoint, and we ship a small control plane reference that uses your KMS. Caveat: on-prem style air-gapped is a separate conversation, takes longer.
[02:35] Michael: Two things — first, what's the SLA when we have a blended route? If we route to hosted by default and only fail-over to dedicated, will latency change?
[02:45] Marco: Good q. If you use a primary dedicated pool for peaks and hosted as fallback, you'll see slightly higher tail latency on fallback because of cold-starts in different pools, but we can configure warm standby and auto-priming. There's a tradeoff: cold standby costs more.
[02:59] Tara: Can we do warm priming on the dedicated pool during predictable windows?
[03:04] Marco: Yes — scheduled warmups or predictive priming based on traffic signals. Also we can do prefix caching for repeated prompts to bring p95 down.
[03:12] Michael: Any quick wins for the immediate p99? The release last week expanded prompts but we can also change our batching parameters.
[03:19] Marco: Short term: tweak batch timeout to prefer smaller latency-sensitive requests, enable aggressive prefix caching for summarization flows, and consider quantized model variants for enrichment heavy jobs. We'll need to benchmark though.
[03:31] Jillian: We'll propose concrete benchmark tests. Marco, can you run a mixed workload benchmark with their sample prompts?
[03:36] Marco: Yes, I'll run a 24h mixed workload with the sample set. I want both latency histograms and token-cost per throughput for hosted vs dedicated.
[03:44] Tara: Great. Also curious about model variants — we use an Llama-like open model. Any recommendation on quantization profiles?
[03:52] Marco: For Llama-family at 4-bit Q4 variants we often see ~1.5-2x perf improvement on seqs under 512 with minimal qualitative regressions. But for >512 sequences you have to watch kernel fidelity. We'll include recommended quant profiles in the benchmark doc.
[04:07] Priya: On security: we need SOC2 documentation, key rotation guarantees, and per-token audit logs. Do you provide HSM-backed KMS options?
[04:17] Jillian: Yes, we can integrate with customer HSM/KMS and provide per-token audit trails retained per your retention policy; some of that is on the private plan. We'll share our security pack.
[04:26] Tara: Who will own the private deployment runbook? We need a runbook to hand to our infra team.
[04:31] Marco: Redwood SEs collaborate on an initial runbook; we can co-author with your SREs. Priya, Marco from Redwood will set a runbook draft after the deep-dive.
[04:40] Priya: Sounds good. Also want to flag throttling behavior — if Redwood returns 429s, what's the recommended backoff?
[04:47] Marco: Exponential jitter backoff for clients; on server side we can also provide queuing tokens and prioritize critical routes. The console supports per-route quotas so you can reserve capacity for high-priority flows.
[04:58] Michael: About cost modeling — in your blended scenario, do you assume the dedicated pool is sized for p99 or for p95?
[05:05] Jillian: Typically you size dedicated for p95 steady-state and use hosted for tail spikes. But for strict p99 SLOs you might make the dedicated pool larger or add warm standby. We'll show both scenarios.
[05:17] Tara: Timeline wise, we're aiming for a pilot before end of Q4. Is that realistic?
[05:21] Marco: Pilot with dedicated pool + routing rules — yes, if we move fast on benchmarks, pricing sign-off, and SOC2 review. Roughly 4-6 weeks for a VPC private pilot depending on procurement.
[05:32] Jillian: Procurement — any gating stakeholders we should know?
[05:36] Michael: Security (Priya), procurement (me), and our CTO wants to see the numbers before signing up for reserved capacity.
[05:44] Jillian: Got it. We'll prepare a one-pager for the CTO with cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:49] Tara: One more question — how do you handle model rollouts and regressions? We need to be sure a new model version won't raise hallucination or latency.
[05:58] Marco: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automated rollback on quality regressions linked to evals. We can tie regressions to your prompt set so the evals run during deploy.
[06:08] Michael: For the benchmark, can you include a run that simulates our enrich job with longer seqs and 20% of calls needing long context?
[06:15] Marco: Yup, we'll parameterize that.
[06:18] Tara: Okay, if you can do the benchmark and the pricing scenarios quickly we'll try to fast-track procurement.
[06:25] Jillian: We'll do that. Quick recap of owners? Marco benchmarks, Jillian pricing + CTO one-pager, Tara to share prompts and traffic CSV, Priya to confirm SOC2 stakeholders.
[06:36] Michael: That works. Any other risks we haven't covered?
[06:39] Priya: Day-2 operations — who gets alerts and runbook access? We need RBAC for internal teams.
[06:45] Marco: RBAC and SSO via SAML are supported; we'll include recommended groups and permissions in the runbook.
[06:51] Tara: Also curious about observability retention costs — the console default retention is 30 days but we may want 90. What's the cost delta?
[06:58] Jillian: We'll put retention pricing in the pricing doc. Longer retention is an add-on.
[07:04] Michael: Can we get a sample export of tracing hooks and per-token cost breakdown?
[07:09] Marco: Yes, included in the benchmark artifact.
[07:12] Tara: Anything else?
[07:14] Jillian: No, wrap up — we'll send the deck with updated numbers by Monday, Marco will kick off the benchmark today, and we'll reconvene with the technical deep-dive week of Oct 25.
[07:24] Marco: One small note: some product names get garbled in transcripts — we call the dedicated product 'Redwood Dedicated' but sometimes show up in logs as 'Redwood Dedicate' — just ignore the typo in older docs.
[07:36] Priya: Haha noted.
[07:39] Jillian: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and share the action items in Slack.
[07:46] Tara: Thanks all, appreciate it.
[07:48] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings on product names, some punctuation and run-on sentences.
